title: Spin Spin Sugar
year_note: The album version is on Becoming X (UK release 19 August 1996). It came out as a single on 3 March 1997, with the Armand van Helden remix on the 12-inch.

notes.made: Chris Corner, Liam Howe and Ian Pickering wrote it, and Kelli Dayton sang it. The album version runs on a driving bass line played on a synthesizer, with a second synth loop turning over above it. For the single, Armand van Helden made a nine-minute 'Dark Garage' mix that has almost nothing to do with the album's mood.
notes.context: The single got to 21 in the UK, but the van Helden mix went to number 1 on the UK Dance chart and 2 on the US Hot Dance Club chart, and it is sometimes credited with bringing speed garage into the mainstream. Music Week complained at the time that the faster radio mix lost the album version's brooding menace. That gap is why the panel argued about it: the version on this list is the slow one, and most people who know the song know the club one.

listen_for.note: The bass is a synthesizer, not a bass guitar, and it pushes the whole track forward on its own.
A second synth loop repeats over the top. Strip the drums out and those two loops are the song.

leads_to.title: Professional Widow (It's Got to Be Big) (Armand's Star Trunk Funkin' Mix)
leads_to.why: The other van Helden remix of that winter, and the one that went to number 1 in the UK: a cousin to the club version of this song.

notes.unverified: Wikipedia categorises it as produced by Flood, but the article text doesn't say so, so I left the producer out.

culture.title: Released March 1997
culture.line: Out on 3 March 1997 as the fourth single from Becoming X, it reached 21 in the UK and number 1 on the UK Dance chart. In the US it hit 87 on the Hot 100 and 2 on Dance Club Songs.

culture.title: Armand van Helden's Dark Garage mix
culture.line: Armand van Helden's nine-minute 'Dark Garage' mix on the UK 12-inch is sometimes credited with pushing speed garage into the mainstream for the first time.
